newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Amity, Pennzoil in gas farmin.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Amity, Pennzoil in gas farmin.

text.p: Amity Oil NL said on Thursday it has entered into a farmin agreement with Pennzoil Exploration Australia Inc whereby Pennzoil can earn an interest in Petroleum Exploration Permit Application 15/94-5 by conducting and funding drilling and workover operations on the Whicher Range gasfield.
Pennzoil is a subsidiary of Pennzoil Co of the U.S.

The Whicher Range field, located in Western Australia and discovered in 1968, holds possible gas resources of more than one trillion cubic feet, but has not been developed due to uneconomic gas flow rates from the low permeability sandstone reservoir.
Pennzoil will apply modern drilling and hydraulic fracture stimulation technology to a two-well assessment of the field, Amity said.
Pennzoil can earn its stake in the permit by performing re-entry, hydraulic fracture stimulation ("fraccing") and testing of the 4,653 metre deep Whicher Range 1 well, it said.
The farmin is subject to the grant of the permit and statutory approvals.
Amity's present interest in the permit application is 58.82 percent.

After completion of farmin obligations by Pennzoil, interests in the permit would be Amity 30.115 percent, GeoPetro Co 14 percent, Pennzoil 44.115 percent and Seven Seas Petroleum Inc unit Seven Seas Petroleum Australia Inc 11.77 percent, Amity said.
Granting of the permit has been delayed by a native title claim lodged in December, 1995 by a group on behalf of the Nyungah Aboriginal people.
Amity said it is negotiating a compensation agreement with the Nyungah.
"Negotiations are proceeding in a spirit of co-operation and Amity is confident that agreement can be reached, allowing the permit to be granted," it said.
